account:
Today has seemed fairly quiet so far. I read my appointment book at town hall, attended morning office hours, and made the scheduled ten o'clock market walk. Several townsfolk said they had no news. Townsfolk 28, 18, and 08 all said the baker had been carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with ordinary bread production; I have seen no evidence of anything unusual behind it. I bought one fresh loaf for lunch.

The only uncertainty is my three o'clock tea appointment. The book describes tea with a neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage but gives neither a name nor an exact cottage. The secretary did not initially know the details and asked who invited me; I had no separate invitation. She took the appointment book and told me she was going to the east-bank cottages to identify the host. I have not yet heard confirmation. I heard her speaking later but could not make out the words, so I cannot infer what she learned.

I briefly saw the builder walking through the plaza carrying a lantern. I tried asking about town business, but the builder had moved beyond talking range and apparently did not hear me. I do not know where the builder was going or why the lantern was being carried.

It is now noon and I am at home for my scheduled lunch. My remaining appointments today are town accounts at the office at thirteen hundred, dockside tea at fifteen hundred, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen hundred.
